reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with my experience at Adrenark Abu Dhabi. I had pre-booked a birthday celebration based on a great previous visit, but what we received this time was unprofessional, unorganized, and far below what was promised.

There were barely any staff at most of the games. Children were standing around waiting, thinking the games were closed because no one was supervising. When I asked two employees near the zip line to help open the slides, they told me to “go call someone” and said it wasn’t their job. This was very unprofessional and shocking, especially when the place knew a group of kids was coming.

Our booking clearly stated that 4–5 PM was for cake, and 5–7 PM was unlimited play. But at 6 PM, while the kids were still playing, the staff suddenly started serving the food — without checking with us — which took around 40 minutes away from their playtime. They later blamed it on “miscommunication,” but they never discussed the timing with us before the party, only after we arrived and were already decorating.

I also paid an extra 1,000 AED for the food that was ordered from an outside vendor. So why would the children lose playtime for food that wasn’t even prepared inside? This made no sense at all.

Because of the poor coordination and lack of staff, the children didn’t get to play many of the main activities — not the slides, not the climbing, not the upper course. This is not what we paid for.

I contacted the team afterward, expecting a proper solution. Instead, they gave excuses and offered only a voucher, which I do not accept. I asked for a partial refund because the service was not delivered as promised, and the value we received was far below what was paid for.

Unfortunately, based on this experience and the way the issue was handled, I cannot recommend Adrenark. I hope they improve their communication, staffing, and professionalism, especially when dealing with children’s events.

reviews.text:
Disappointing experience. My daughter’s height was checked at reception and we were told she was eligible for rafting and kayaking, so we purchased the tickets accordingly. We had also checked the requirements from home before coming. However, at the activity areas, her height was checked again and she was refused, resulting in a lot of wasted time.
We were then asked to downgrade to basic splash activities, but we traveled all the way to Al Ain specifically for the advertised rafting activities, not for the basic splash options. I fully respect safety rules and would never expect my daughter to participate in anything unsafe. The issue was not the safety restriction, but the lack of clear communication and responsibility at the start. I hope the park improves coordination and accuracy in eligibility checks so other families do not face a similar situation.

reviews.text:
I visited Al Qattara Arts Centre in Al Ain, and it was such a peaceful and inspiring experience. 🌿
The place beautifully combines traditional Emirati architecture with a touch of modern creativity. As you walk through the corridors, you can feel the connection between history and art in every corner.

The centre features various art galleries showcasing works by both local and international artists. They also offer workshops and cultural programs that are perfect for anyone interested in learning or exploring art.

The staff are welcoming and knowledgeable, and the whole space is calm, clean, and well-maintained. It’s truly a cultural gem in Al Ain — ideal for art lovers, photographers, and anyone who enjoys quiet, meaningful experiences. 🎨✨

reviews.text:
Al Qattara Arts Center, Oman – Inspiring Investment & Tourism in Baku, Azerbaijan

"Visiting Al Qattara Arts Center in Oman was an inspiring experience. The center showcases contemporary and traditional art, hosts engaging exhibitions, and provides a creative environment for both artists and visitors. It demonstrates how culture, innovation, and community engagement can create a vibrant destination.

Similarly, Baku, Azerbaijan is emerging as a hub for arts, culture, and investment opportunities. With its growing economy, expanding tourism sector, and investor-friendly environment, Baku provides entrepreneurs, investors, and tourists a unique platform to explore cultural, artistic, and business ventures. Just as Al Qattara Arts Center fosters creativity and engagement, Baku offers fertile ground for innovative ventures and investment.

For those inspired by artistic and cultural excellence, Baku, Azerbaijan is a prime destination for tourism, investment, and entrepreneurial growth."

I recently had the pleasure of visiting the Annex Lounge at Edition Hotel Abu Dhabi, and I must say, it was an absolutely amazing experience. From the moment I stepped through the doors, I was enchanted by the cozy and classy atmosphere that exuded elegance and comfort.

The first thing that stood out to me was the incredible vibes that filled the air. The lounge had a fantastic energy, making it the perfect place to unwind and enjoy a memorable evening. The music played by the talented Dj and live singer was nothing short of perfect. The diverse playlist catered to different tastes and moods, delivering a seamless blend of upbeat tunes and laid-back melodies. It truly added to the lively ambiance of the lounge.

The Annex Lounge boasts a super fancy setting, which only added to the overall experience. The stylish decor and chic furniture created an ambiance that was both sophisticated and welcoming. Every aspect of the lounge oozed class and attention to detail.

The staff at Annex Lounge deserve a special mention for their exceptional service. From the moment I arrived, I was greeted warmly and made to feel like a valued guest. The staff members were attentive, friendly, and went above and beyond to ensure that my experience was nothing short of extraordinary.

As I reflect upon my time at the Annex Lounge, I can confidently say that it surpassed all of my expectations. It's undoubtedly a place that I would recommend to anyone seeking a memorable and enjoyable evening. Whether you're looking to celebrate a special occasion or simply unwind after a long day, Annex Lounge is the perfect destination.

In conclusion, if you're in Abu Dhabi and craving a cozy, classy, and vibrant experience, make sure to visit the Annex Lounge at Edition Hotel. With its great vibes, perfect music, super fancy ambiance, and lovely staff, your time there is guaranteed to be exceptional. I know I will definitely be returning for more unforgettable moments.
reviews.author: MWK Nirmani

reviews.text: Annex gave me an unforgettable 33rd birthday with all my lady friends. Thank you to  Sinead (hostess) and Melanie (waitress)! The service was out of this world and the actual vibe, look & music was classy and so much fun. Will definitely be going back for another friends birthday.

reviews.text:
We had our company’s Christmas Party / Year-End Party in the ANNEX at the roof top last December 10, 2021. We availed a 3-hour package (5:30PM - 8:00PM) for food and drinks. Non Alcoholic package for AED 288 per person and Alcholic package for AED 295 per person. As per our organizer, we were promised that the food and drinks will be continuously served for 3 hours.

The venue was beautiful. The ambiance was great and the setting was picturesque as you have the view of the Al Bateen Marina.

The music was terrible. It’s not a music that you can dance to. We requested if the music can be changed but to no avail.

Some of the food tasted good but the serving was not enough. The maximum number of people per table was 10 people. For example: they only served 1 bowl of nachos for 10 people which was not enough. We asked them if we could get some more and they said that we will get it again as the menu is on rotation.

The serving time for food and drinks was very disappointing. They would serve food for maximum of 1 hour and it was just a 3-hour package. It was hard to order drinks as well as the waiters seem to be busy or not around. A lot of us were complaining that they were hungry from the long wait to be served with food.

There were a couple of security men and waiters that were rude and seem to be unbothered by our concerns and disappointments.

The last order for drinks was at 8PM and we were told that it can only be one drink per person. Which was ridiculous!

By the time it was 8:30PM we were told that we have to leave immediately as our time is over and that there was another group of people coming. Some of us weren’t even finish with our drinks and food yet.

I thought that the amount that we paid was not worth of the amount of food and service that we got. As much as we enjoyed each other’s company, the experience and service that we got was not up to par.
reviews.author: Earl Marquez

reviews.text: It was a work Christmas Party booked at night last December 10, 2021 with package of 10 food presented (appetizers and mains). Paid for 3 hours to free flow drinks. Having the drink was not a problem and it was the good thing happened. Though the most disappointing part was the SLOW food service and even the expectation of having a taste of ALL the food being offered and paid was NOT being delivered. I have tasted 4 out of 10 and it was even being shared on the table not even served individually. The expectation of EVEN having a taste of the at least majority of the appetizing food was NOT accomplished. Paying 295aed was not only looking for drinks/alcohol but also a least a satisfying food service. I hope services will get better. Place was intimate and clean, lovely personnel sofia, perez and chris but it was Just Unsatisfactory FOOD service for the amount I paid for it.

reviews.text:
I recently had the pleasure of visiting the Annex Lounge at Edition Hotel Abu Dhabi, and I must say, it was an absolutely amazing experience. From the moment I stepped through the doors, I was enchanted by the cozy and classy atmosphere that exuded elegance and comfort.

The first thing that stood out to me was the incredible vibes that filled the air. The lounge had a fantastic energy, making it the perfect place to unwind and enjoy a memorable evening. The music played by the talented Dj and live singer was nothing short of perfect. The diverse playlist catered to different tastes and moods, delivering a seamless blend of upbeat tunes and laid-back melodies. It truly added to the lively ambiance of the lounge.

The Annex Lounge boasts a super fancy setting, which only added to the overall experience. The stylish decor and chic furniture created an ambiance that was both sophisticated and welcoming. Every aspect of the lounge oozed class and attention to detail.

The staff at Annex Lounge deserve a special mention for their exceptional service. From the moment I arrived, I was greeted warmly and made to feel like a valued guest. The staff members were attentive, friendly, and went above and beyond to ensure that my experience was nothing short of extraordinary.

As I reflect upon my time at the Annex Lounge, I can confidently say that it surpassed all of my expectations. It's undoubtedly a place that I would recommend to anyone seeking a memorable and enjoyable evening. Whether you're looking to celebrate a special occasion or simply unwind after a long day, Annex Lounge is the perfect destination.

In conclusion, if you're in Abu Dhabi and craving a cozy, classy, and vibrant experience, make sure to visit the Annex Lounge at Edition Hotel. With its great vibes, perfect music, super fancy ambiance, and lovely staff, your time there is guaranteed to be exceptional. I know I will definitely be returning for more unforgettable moments.

reviews.text: Annex gave me an unforgettable 33rd birthday with all my lady friends. Thank you to  Sinead (hostess) and Melanie (waitress)! The service was out of this world and the actual vibe, look & music was classy and so much fun. Will definitely be going back for another friends birthday.

offers a great range of art supplies, from sketchbooks and paints to canvases and specialty materials. The store is beautifully organized, making it easy to browse and find exactly what you need. There is also an art studio for those wishing to learn.

The staff are knowledgeable, friendly, and always ready to help you choose the right tools for your projects. It’s a great spot for students, hobby artists, and professionals. Convenient location inside Boutik Mall, with parking available and other shops nearby.

A must-visit if you're looking for quality art supplies on Reem Island.
reviews.author: Shahida Alvarado

reviews.text:
This place is honestly my favorite ever! If you love pottery or anything art related, you’ll fall in love with it. It’s super organized and has everything you can imagine from clay, glazes, and tools to other art supplies too.

The studio inside is sooo nice and peaceful. It’s clean, cozy, and just has the perfect creative vibe.

And honestly, the staff is a big part of why I love this place so much. They’re always welcoming and really make you feel comfortable to ask anything. Even if I ask a lot of questions, they never get annoyed they explain everything so clearly and kindly. You can tell they actually know what they’re talking about and they genuinely want to help. Whether it’s advice about firing, glazing, or choosing the right materials, They’re patient, professional, and super friendly

It’s honestly the perfect place for any Artist whether you’re just starting or already deep into it.
reviews.author: maha alrayssi

reviews.text: What am amazing experience! It was our first time to try pottery making.  The place was rather easy to find. Located in Shams. We were sceptical about getting a slab of clay and working our way through it like dough but turns out I think id prefer to do this than the turn table but they have both options plus many more and I'm eager to try them out slowly over time.  We spent roughly two hours from rolling the slab of clay to painting and adding finishing touches.  Final product in two weeks after they fire / glaze them in the oven.  Can't wait to be back again.

I had a very disappointing experience with this store. After waiting over three months for my order, I was informed at the last minute about a price increase from 88 AED to 98 AED for the glaze. This information was not communicated when I placed my order via WhatsApp. I was only asked to confirm the order while I was at the airport, making it impossible to review the details properly.

Additionally, their website clearly states that orders over 200 AED qualify for free delivery. Despite spending 600 AED, I was told I need to pay an additional 50 AED for delivery. This lack of transparency and poor communication is unacceptable. I do not plan to order from or visit this store again unless they resolve these issues.

reviews.text: Our experience at Bounce Marina Mall was made truly special thanks to Coach Zayed Al Menhali. From the very first visit, he welcomed my kids Malik (8) and Maryam (7) with warmth and encouragement, making them feel both safe and excited. Incredibly, he managed to teach them a front flip on their very first session, along with other fun skills that boosted their confidence. What impressed me most was his attentiveness to safety, his professionalism, and the genuine care he showed in tracking their progress across visits. His kindness and welcoming nature reflect not just the positive spirit of Bounce, but also the hospitality of the UAE. A truly outstanding coach who made every visit memorable. تجربتنا في باونس مارينا مول كانت مميزة للغاية بفضل المدرب زايد المنهالي. فمنذ الزيارة الأولى استقبل أطفالي (مالك ثمان سنوات، ومريم سبع سنوات) بكل ترحيب وتشجيع ، مما جعلهم يشعرون بالأمان والحماس في الوقت نفسه. وبشكل مذهل تمكن من تعليمهم الشقلبة الأمامية خلال الحصة الأولى، إلى جانب مهارات ممتعة أخرى عززت ثقتهم بأنفسهم. ما أعجبني أكثر هو حرصه الكبير على السلامة، واحترافيته العالية، واهتمامه الصادق بمتابعة تقدمهم خلال الزيارات. لقد عكست طيبته وحسن استقباله الروح الإيجابية لباونس، وتميز اللباقة والضيافة الإماراتية. مدرب رائع بالفعل جعل كل زيارة لا تُنسى.

My younger son trains with Coach Jerome, who is a great coach for ages 3-5. His energy is infectious for the little ones, and he approaches each and every class with a fun and positive attitude. He’s great at keeping the little ones engaged and can quickly notice when they’re ready to move on to the next activity.

My older son is with Coach Kishan, who has become his favourite mentor, to the point where he missed him all summer. Coach Kishan has a magical way of making every child feel super seen and loved, and is amazing at creating a sense of camaraderie and belonging. His energy is also contagious.

Both coaches have been instrumental in teaching my sons the right skills needed to be able to safely do tricks like flips and parkour. BFA has been an incredible way for them to learn skills in resilience, agility and coordination.

reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and unprofessional experience.

I was denied entry solely because I did not have my physical passport with me, despite the fact that I was coming abroad, properly dressed, and accompanied by friends who were all allowed in without any issue. I was the only one singled out — none of my friends were asked for the same requirement.

What makes this even more unacceptable is that I did have a digital copy of my ID, which was explicitly refused, with the explanation that digital IDs are only accepted for UAE holders. This is not only inconsistent, but clearly discriminatory.

The door staff, Mariam, enforced this selectively and without professionalism or basic courtesy. If this is truly a policy, it should be applied equally to everyone, not based on nationality or personal judgment.

For a venue that presents itself as welcoming, this behavior is outdated, biased, and embarrassing. Hospitality should never involve singling out or humiliating guests.

Plenty of places manage entry policies with fairness and respect. Unfortunately, this one did not.

I visited Central in Yas Bay during the 54th Eid Al Ittihad celebrations, and it was truly one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in Abu Dhabi. The restaurant has an incredible front-row view of the Yas Bay fireworks — genuinely the perfect spot to enjoy the show without any obstruction. The atmosphere was festive, vibrant, and beautifully managed despite the huge crowds that night.

A special shout-out goes to the manager, Tobi (I believe that’s the correct spelling). His professionalism, warmth, and attention to detail elevated the entire experience. He checked on every table personally, made sure we were comfortable, and even helped us get the best view right on time for the fireworks. You rarely find hospitality like this anymore — he made us feel genuinely welcomed and well taken care of.

The service was smooth, the food was great, and the vibe was unmatched. If you’re looking for a place to enjoy Yas Bay views, great food, and top-tier service, Central is 100% worth it. I’ll definitely be coming back!

reviews.text:
Extremely disappointing and unprofessional experience.

I was denied entry solely because I did not have my physical passport with me, despite the fact that I was coming abroad, properly dressed, and accompanied by friends who were all allowed in without any issue. I was the only one singled out — none of my friends were asked for the same requirement.

What makes this even more unacceptable is that I did have a digital copy of my ID, which was explicitly refused, with the explanation that digital IDs are only accepted for UAE holders. This is not only inconsistent, but clearly discriminatory.

The door staff, Mariam, enforced this selectively and without professionalism or basic courtesy. If this is truly a policy, it should be applied equally to everyone, not based on nationality or personal judgment.

For a venue that presents itself as welcoming, this behavior is outdated, biased, and embarrassing. Hospitality should never involve singling out or humiliating guests.

Plenty of places manage entry policies with fairness and respect. Unfortunately, this one did not.

I visited Central in Yas Bay during the 54th Eid Al Ittihad celebrations, and it was truly one of the best dining experiences I’ve had in Abu Dhabi. The restaurant has an incredible front-row view of the Yas Bay fireworks — genuinely the perfect spot to enjoy the show without any obstruction. The atmosphere was festive, vibrant, and beautifully managed despite the huge crowds that night.

A special shout-out goes to the manager, Tobi (I believe that’s the correct spelling). His professionalism, warmth, and attention to detail elevated the entire experience. He checked on every table personally, made sure we were comfortable, and even helped us get the best view right on time for the fireworks. You rarely find hospitality like this anymore — he made us feel genuinely welcomed and well taken care of.

The service was smooth, the food was great, and the vibe was unmatched. If you’re looking for a place to enjoy Yas Bay views, great food, and top-tier service, Central is 100% worth it. I’ll definitely be coming back!

reviews.text:
Terrible terrible experience.

Extremely disappointing customer service and poor coordination.

I had a very frustrating experience with them, mainly due to their call center’s incompetence and lack of accountability.

I had a valid voucher and called the customer service center to ask how to book a session. I was told I could either book in person or that they could reserve the session for me over the phone. To avoid inconvenience, I chose the phone option. Given my doubts of their incompetence, I called multiple times to confirm that my session was booked and was reassured each time that my request had been noted and processed.

On the day of the session, I arrived only to find out that nothing had been booked at all. I wasted a significant amount of time going back and forth between the venue reception and the call center, and no solution was reached.

To be fair, the venue reception staff were polite and professional and offered a complimentary session and a reschedule. However, by that point my experience was already ruined, and I declined.

The call center experience was unacceptable: during one call, an agent read a note that clearly stated my request (“Book L2 session…”), but after being put on hold for a long time and calling again, I was told that I must have “heard wrong.” This is despite the fact that I had called more than once specifically to confirm the booking.

Now, instead of enjoying the experience I planned for, I’m forced into a long, tedious refund process for something that failed due to their internal mismanagement.

Great facility, but severely undermined by an unreliable and inconsistent call center. I would not recommend booking anything through phone support.

reviews.text:
Terrible terrible experience.

Extremely disappointing customer service and poor coordination.

I had a very frustrating experience with them, mainly due to their call center’s incompetence and lack of accountability.

I had a valid voucher and called the customer service center to ask how to book a session. I was told I could either book in person or that they could reserve the session for me over the phone. To avoid inconvenience, I chose the phone option. Given my doubts of their incompetence, I called multiple times to confirm that my session was booked and was reassured each time that my request had been noted and processed.

On the day of the session, I arrived only to find out that nothing had been booked at all. I wasted a significant amount of time going back and forth between the venue reception and the call center, and no solution was reached.

To be fair, the venue reception staff were polite and professional and offered a complimentary session and a reschedule. However, by that point my experience was already ruined, and I declined.

The call center experience was unacceptable: during one call, an agent read a note that clearly stated my request (“Book L2 session…”), but after being put on hold for a long time and calling again, I was told that I must have “heard wrong.” This is despite the fact that I had called more than once specifically to confirm the booking.

Now, instead of enjoying the experience I planned for, I’m forced into a long, tedious refund process for something that failed due to their internal mismanagement.

Great facility, but severely undermined by an unreliable and inconsistent call center. I would not recommend booking anything through phone support.

reviews.text:
Qasr Al Hosn & Cultural Foundation: A Journey Through Time and Creativity ✨

Qasr Al Hosn is one of Abu Dhabi’s most iconic cultural landmarks, standing as a testament to the emirate’s rich history. Originally built as a watchtower in the 18th century, it later evolved into a fortress and the residence of the ruling Al Nahyan family. Today, it is a beautifully restored museum that narrates Abu Dhabi’s transformation from a small fishing village to a global metropolis.👍

⭐️Adjacent to Qasr Al Hosn is the Cultural Foundation, a hub for artistic expression and learning. The foundation offers a variety of workshops and exhibitions that celebrate art in its many forms. Visitors can participate in oil painting, acrylic and watercolor classes, painting on silk, sculpture, ceramics, photography, jewelry-making, sewing, and Arabic calligraphy. These workshops cater to both beginners and seasoned artists, making it a perfect place for anyone looking to explore their creativity.

📚The Study Lounge provides a peaceful environment for reading, research, and self-improvement, while the Theatre and Music programs bring performances that range from traditional Arabic shows to contemporary international productions. The venue itself is a masterpiece of modern architecture blended with Emirati heritage, offering an inspiring setting for learning and cultural appreciation. Convenient parking ensures an easy visit for all guests.

Another Cultural Gem: House of Artisans 🎨

For those interested in exploring the traditional crafts of the UAE, the House of Artisans is a must-visit destination. Located near Qasr Al Hosn, this cultural center is dedicated to preserving and promoting Emirati craftsmanship.

The House of Artisans is not just a place to observe but also to engage with skilled artisans who keep these traditions alive. The experience offers a deeper appreciation of the UAE’s cultural heritage while providing an opportunity to create unique handmade souvenirs.

With its interactive experiences and rich storytelling, the House of Artisans is an excellent complement to a visit to Qasr Al Hosn, making for a well-rounded cultural journey through Abu Dhabi’s past and present.

Immerse yourself in the heart of Abu Dhabi's cultural scene at the Cultural Foundation! This vibrant hub celebrates the UAE's rich heritage and artistic expression through a variety of offerings:

- Art Exhibitions: The Cultural Foundation showcases a cutting-edge visual arts program featuring both local and international artists.

Performing Arts: Catch world-class contemporary performances, including music, dance, and theater,  in the renovated 900-seat theater.

Abu Dhabi Children's Library: A one-of-a-kind  5,250-square-meter  facility designed as a life-size pop-up book, perfect for sparking a love of reading in young minds.

- Al Marsam Al Hor: This educational center offers a variety of classes and workshops for all ages and skill levels, fostering artistic exploration.

In short: The Cultural Foundation is a must-visit for anyone seeking a taste of Abu Dhabi's cultural riches.

reviews.text:
Rating: ★★★★☆ (4.0/5)

A truly unique automotive experience nestled in the desert sands of Al Dhafra, the Emirates National Auto Museum is a testament to one man's passion for vehicles.  Housing over 200 cars from the personal collection of His Highness Sheikh Hamad Bin Hamdan Al Nahyan, this pyramid-shaped museum offers visitors a glimpse into an eclectic array of automobiles, from classic American muscle cars to custom-built off-roaders.

Highlights:

Diverse Collection: The museum boasts a wide range of vehicles, including the Sheikh's famous "Rainbow Collection" of Mercedes-Benz cars, each painted in a different hue.

Record-Breaking Exhibits: Marvel at the world's largest motorized model car—a 4:1 scale replica of a Willys Jeep—and the massive Dodge Power Wagon, both of which are fully functional.

Photogenic Exterior: Before even entering, visitors are greeted by a retired passenger jet and the iconic globe-shaped mobile home, offering ample photo opportunities.

Considerations:

Remote Location: Situated approximately 45 kilometers south of Abu Dhabi city, reaching the museum requires a bit of a drive through the desert.

Limited Amenities: The museum lacks on-site dining options, so it's advisable to bring your own refreshments.

Maintenance: Some vehicles show signs of wear, and additional informational placards could enhance the visitor experience.

Visitor Tips:

Operating Hours: Open daily from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM.

Admission: Entry fee is AED 50, with free admission for children under 10.

Best Time to Visit: To avoid the midday heat, consider visiting in the morning or late afternoon.

Final Thoughts: The Emirates National Auto Museum offers a fascinating journey through automotive history and innovation.  While it may not have the polish of more conventional museums, its unique exhibits and the sheer passion behind the collection make it a must-visit for car enthusiasts and curious travelers alike.

My husband and I visited the museum early on a weekend morning, around 10 AM. We paid for both of us at the entrance (I don’t recall the exact amount), and since there were no other visitors at that time, we were able to park close to the museum building.

We visited in April, and it was already quite warm—so I highly recommend bringing a bottle of water with you. The museum itself is spacious, with a fascinating collection of unique and antique cars. Be prepared to walk a lot to explore everything!

Even in the morning, it felt a bit hot inside. I believe the air conditioning system is a bit outdated and doesn’t cool the space very well, which made the visit a bit uncomfortable at times.

That said, I really enjoyed the overall experience. While it might not be the kind of place you’d return to multiple times, it’s definitely worth a visit if you’re interested in automotive history or just want to see something different. I’d recommend it for car enthusiasts and curious minds alike.

It was a unqie animal experience where you get to interact with animals, feed them. Also get to eat alongside the animal kingdoms. Some of the species you can look for are Giraffes, Sea lions, Black Panther, Leopards, white Tiger, Hippo, Hyenas, Lion and some local species.
My favourite was Giraffe feeding, Hippo and Hyena experience and also a Birthday outing including a small cake cutting at the Hide restaurant. Its definitely worth a visit if you have kids or if you havent got chance to see these species!

Tips:
1. Visit during the evening hours. Avoid morning time due to heat as most of the animals are in their den.
2. Avoid peak summer timings as its an outdoor park.
3. Resort for stay available just in case your visiting from a long distance inside the zoo.

reviews.text:
The zoo is an absolutely beautiful and enjoyable place. It is, without a doubt, one of the best zoos in terms of care, animal diversity, and engaging activities. Every visit feels exciting, and I never get tired of coming here. The environment is well-maintained, and you can clearly see the effort put into the animals’ well-being and the overall experience.

However, the food prices are extremely exaggerated. They are not just double the normal prices, but triple or even more. What makes it even more unreasonable is that bringing food from outside is not allowed. This policy simply does not make sense.

Paying 175 AED for only four ice creams is unacceptable — this amount can easily cover a full meal at one of the best restaurants outside the zoo. I genuinely wonder whether consumer protection authorities are aware of such pricing practices, because this level of cost is not logical or fair for visitors.

reviews.text:
Experienced Etihad Arena while working with the SolanaFloor team during Solana Breakpoint 2025. We weren’t part of the main event crew, but had our own glass booth at the back where we ran live streams for three days with multiple speakers.
Spending long hours inside the arena really shows how well the space is built. It’s big, but doesn’t feel chaotic. Sound was clear across the venue, which is super important when you’re doing live talks and streams. The screens, lighting, and overall setup made it easy to run content smoothly without technical friction.
From a media and streaming perspective, the venue handled scale really well. Crowd movement was mostly smooth, and even with everything happening at once, things stayed organised. Staff and security were helpful and easy to work with, which always matters during live production.
The arena stayed clean throughout the event, even during peak hours. Facilities were solid and easy to access. Overall, Etihad Arena felt reliable, modern, and built for large global events.
Covering Solana Breakpoint from here was a great experience for us at SolanaFloor. Definitely a venue that supports high-quality events and media work.

reviews.text: Enjoyed the Arijit singh concert in etihad arena. EXHILARATING EXPERIENCE 😊💗
reviews.author: NATASHA F P

reviews.text:
Last evening’s Arijit Singh concert at Etihad Arena, Abu Dhabi was nothing short of epic. From the very first note to the final encore, it was a musical journey that showcased why Arijit Singh is regarded as one of the finest vocalists of our time.
What stood out most was his vocal mastery and stamina. Singing continuously for nearly five hours, he remained flawless throughout—never once sounding strained or shaky. His control over his voice is truly unmatched, and every song was delivered with depth, emotion, and precision.
Equally impressive was the orchestra. Their coordination with Arijit was seamless, elevating every performance. The synergy between the musicians and the singer created an immersive experience that held the audience spellbound.
Arijit Singh’s humility deserves special mention. Despite being a global icon, he remained grounded and gracious throughout the evening. He patiently acknowledged requests and warmly interacted with guests, making a sincere effort to ensure that everyone felt included and valued before the concert concluded. This generosity of spirit is rare and speaks volumes about his character.
So captivating was the performance that at one point, I genuinely thought the concert had concluded and briefly stepped out—only to hear him begin “Sapphire.” I immediately rushed back in and stayed for yet another hour, completely mesmerized once again.
As for the venue, Etihad Arena continues to be an impressive space for large-scale events. That said, some logistical aspects could perhaps be smoother. There were noticeable queues for food, beverages, and washrooms, and the parking rerouting required a fair amount of patience. These are understandable challenges during high-capacity events, and with such overwhelming attendance, they are areas that could be further optimized in the future.
In the end, words fall short when describing Arijit Singh’s performance. No matter how much praise is given, it still feels insufficient. It was a perfect evening, marked by extraordinary music, heartfelt performances, and an artist whose talent is matched only by his humility.
A truly unforgettable concert. 🎶

reviews.text:
Absolutely disappointed and heartbroken by my experience at Falcon Hospital.

I contacted them about my cat’s blocked bladder—a serious emergency. I was driving in from Dubai to Abu Dhabi, and clearly told them I could only reach after 6 PM. They confirmed it was fine under emergency hours and said it would cost around 275 AED for the visit and possibly around 3,000 AED for treatment, which I was ready to pay.

When I arrived, already stressed and scared for my cat, I asked to see the vet first. But instead of compassion, I was told bluntly by the receptionist to pay 3,000 upfront before the doctor would even see my cat. I asked how that was possible without even examining him—they had already made up the bill.

When the vet finally came out, his attitude was unbelievably cold and dismissive. He told me he “sees a thousand cases like mine every day” and refused to even touch my cat until I paid. I cannot express how awful that felt, standing there holding a suffering animal and being treated like a transaction.

And guess what? It wasn’t even what I feared. The condition was completely different. My cat is doing well now, but not because of their care—because I insisted on real answers and got him help. I ended up paying nearly 5,000 AED, and money wasn’t the issue—I was ready to do whatever it took.
But what I wanted was empathy, professionalism, and a vet who would talk to me like I was a human and my cat was a life—not a price tag.

Falcon Hospital failed me in every possible way that day.
You don’t treat pet owners like this in an emergency.
And you definitely don’t treat animals like that.

reviews.text:
أنا مربي قطط ومنقذ لها، لدي أكثر من 30 قط، وتعاملت مع أغلب العيادات البيطرية في أبوظبي. وكأي مربي، أعتبر قططي أفرادًا من عائلتي وليسوا مجرد حيوانات أليفة.

أشارككم هذه التجربة المؤلمة التي حصلت لي مع مستشفى الصقور البيطري من هذا المنطلق الإنساني.
في إحدى الليالي، أنقذت قطًا من الشارع وكان في حالة حرجة. تواصلت مع المستشفى وأبلغوني أن الطبيب المناوب سيصل خلال نصف ساعة، فتوجهت فورًا بالقط إليهم. عند الوصول، كنت مضطرًا للعودة إلى عملي، وطلب مني الممرض دفع أكثر من ألف درهم كدفعة مقدمة قبل حتى أن يصل الطبيب أو يبدأ أي علاج.

لم تكن لدي مشكلة في الدفع، ولكن لسوء الحظ نسيت محفظتي. طلبت منهم أن يبدأوا بالعلاج وسأعود صباحًا لتسوية المبلغ، خاصة أن حياة القط كانت في خطر. لكنهم رفضوا استلام الحالة، رغم أنهم أخذوا القط إلى غرفة العلاج، وأصروا أن التعليمات من الإدارة تقضي بعدم استقبال أي حالة دون دفع مسبق.

اضطررت إلى أخذ القط إلى عيادة خاصة أخرى، ورغم أنهم ليسوا جهة حكومية، قبلوا الحالة فورًا وتعاملوا معها بإنسانية. لكن للأسف كان الأوان قد فات لإنقاذه.

رسالتي من هذه التجربة: إذا كنت تحب حيوانك الأليف وتعتبره فردًا من عائلتك، فلا أنصحك بالتوجه إلى مستشفى الصقور، خصوصًا في الحالات الحرجة. فبناءً على تجربتي وتجارب آخرين، حتى الحالات الروتينية قد تتحول إلى خسارة بسبب سوء الإدارة وقلة التعاطف.
ما يهمهم أولًا وأخيرًا هو تحصيل المال، وليس إنقاذ الأرواح.

قلبي ما زال يتألم على ما حدث، وأتمنى ألا يمر أحد بهذه التجربة. رجاءً، أخبروا أصدقاءكم ومحبي الحيوانات بعدم التعامل معهم.

I'm a cat rescuer , with over 30 cats under my care. I’ve dealt with most veterinary clinics across Abu Dhabi, and like any true pet lover, I consider my cats family — not just pets.

I'm sharing this painful experience with Falcon Veterinary Hospital from this perspective.

One night, I rescued a cat from the street in a critical condition. I called the hospital and was told the on-call doctor would arrive within 30 minutes, so I rushed the cat to them. Upon arrival, I had to return to work shortly after, but the attending nurse demanded an upfront payment of over AED 1,000 — before the doctor even arrived or treatment had started.

I was fully ready to pay, but unfortunately, I had forgotten my wallet. I kindly requested they begin treatment and promised to return in the morning to settle the bill, knowing the cat’s life was at risk. However, they refused to accept the case, despite already taking the cat into the treatment room, citing "management policy" that no treatment can start without prior payment.

I had no choice but to take the cat to a private clinic I work with — they are not even a government entity, yet they accepted the emergency immediately and showed empathy. Sadly, by the time we got there, it was too late to save the cat.

My message is this: if you truly love your pet and consider them family, I strongly advise against going to Falcon Vet Hospital, especially in emergencies. Based on my experience and that of others, even routine visits can lead to tragedy due to lack of compassion and poor management.

Their top priority is not the wellbeing of your pet — it’s your wallet.

My heart still aches for the loss of my cat. I hope no one else has to go through what I did. Please warn your loved ones and fellow animal lovers not to go there.

Absolutely disappointed and heartbroken by my experience at Falcon Hospital.

I contacted them about my cat’s blocked bladder—a serious emergency. I was driving in from Dubai to Abu Dhabi, and clearly told them I could only reach after 6 PM. They confirmed it was fine under emergency hours and said it would cost around 275 AED for the visit and possibly around 3,000 AED for treatment, which I was ready to pay.

When I arrived, already stressed and scared for my cat, I asked to see the vet first. But instead of compassion, I was told bluntly by the receptionist to pay 3,000 upfront before the doctor would even see my cat. I asked how that was possible without even examining him—they had already made up the bill.

When the vet finally came out, his attitude was unbelievably cold and dismissive. He told me he “sees a thousand cases like mine every day” and refused to even touch my cat until I paid. I cannot express how awful that felt, standing there holding a suffering animal and being treated like a transaction.

And guess what? It wasn’t even what I feared. The condition was completely different. My cat is doing well now, but not because of their care—because I insisted on real answers and got him help. I ended up paying nearly 5,000 AED, and money wasn’t the issue—I was ready to do whatever it took.
But what I wanted was empathy, professionalism, and a vet who would talk to me like I was a human and my cat was a life—not a price tag.

Falcon Hospital failed me in every possible way that day.
You don’t treat pet owners like this in an emergency.
And you definitely don’t treat animals like that.

أنا مربي قطط ومنقذ لها، لدي أكثر من 30 قط، وتعاملت مع أغلب العيادات البيطرية في أبوظبي. وكأي مربي، أعتبر قططي أفرادًا من عائلتي وليسوا مجرد حيوانات أليفة.

أشارككم هذه التجربة المؤلمة التي حصلت لي مع مستشفى الصقور البيطري من هذا المنطلق الإنساني.
في إحدى الليالي، أنقذت قطًا من الشارع وكان في حالة حرجة. تواصلت مع المستشفى وأبلغوني أن الطبيب المناوب سيصل خلال نصف ساعة، فتوجهت فورًا بالقط إليهم. عند الوصول، كنت مضطرًا للعودة إلى عملي، وطلب مني الممرض دفع أكثر من ألف درهم كدفعة مقدمة قبل حتى أن يصل الطبيب أو يبدأ أي علاج.

لم تكن لدي مشكلة في الدفع، ولكن لسوء الحظ نسيت محفظتي. طلبت منهم أن يبدأوا بالعلاج وسأعود صباحًا لتسوية المبلغ، خاصة أن حياة القط كانت في خطر. لكنهم رفضوا استلام الحالة، رغم أنهم أخذوا القط إلى غرفة العلاج، وأصروا أن التعليمات من الإدارة تقضي بعدم استقبال أي حالة دون دفع مسبق.

اضطررت إلى أخذ القط إلى عيادة خاصة أخرى، ورغم أنهم ليسوا جهة حكومية، قبلوا الحالة فورًا وتعاملوا معها بإنسانية. لكن للأسف كان الأوان قد فات لإنقاذه.

رسالتي من هذه التجربة: إذا كنت تحب حيوانك الأليف وتعتبره فردًا من عائلتك، فلا أنصحك بالتوجه إلى مستشفى الصقور، خصوصًا في الحالات الحرجة. فبناءً على تجربتي وتجارب آخرين، حتى الحالات الروتينية قد تتحول إلى خسارة بسبب سوء الإدارة وقلة التعاطف.
ما يهمهم أولًا وأخيرًا هو تحصيل المال، وليس إنقاذ الأرواح.

قلبي ما زال يتألم على ما حدث، وأتمنى ألا يمر أحد بهذه التجربة. رجاءً، أخبروا أصدقاءكم ومحبي الحيوانات بعدم التعامل معهم.

I'm a cat rescuer , with over 30 cats under my care. I’ve dealt with most veterinary clinics across Abu Dhabi, and like any true pet lover, I consider my cats family — not just pets.

I'm sharing this painful experience with Falcon Veterinary Hospital from this perspective.

One night, I rescued a cat from the street in a critical condition. I called the hospital and was told the on-call doctor would arrive within 30 minutes, so I rushed the cat to them. Upon arrival, I had to return to work shortly after, but the attending nurse demanded an upfront payment of over AED 1,000 — before the doctor even arrived or treatment had started.

I was fully ready to pay, but unfortunately, I had forgotten my wallet. I kindly requested they begin treatment and promised to return in the morning to settle the bill, knowing the cat’s life was at risk. However, they refused to accept the case, despite already taking the cat into the treatment room, citing "management policy" that no treatment can start without prior payment.

I had no choice but to take the cat to a private clinic I work with — they are not even a government entity, yet they accepted the emergency immediately and showed empathy. Sadly, by the time we got there, it was too late to save the cat.

My message is this: if you truly love your pet and consider them family, I strongly advise against going to Falcon Vet Hospital, especially in emergencies. Based on my experience and that of others, even routine visits can lead to tragedy due to lack of compassion and poor management.

Their top priority is not the wellbeing of your pet — it’s your wallet.

My heart still aches for the loss of my cat. I hope no one else has to go through what I did. Please warn your loved ones and fellow animal lovers not to go there.

We went on a Monday. Got in line at 11:40 and didn’t actually get on the ride until 15:30. (Screen said to wait 100 mins but turned out to be 230 mins) Compared to Ferrari Land in Spain, the queue management here felt much worse.

Formula Rossa itself is great, but unless you have Quick Pass, be ready for very long waiting times and plan your visit carefully.

reviews.text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.
reviews.author: Anand Gupta

reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

reviews.text:
It's a straight up money printing machine to make up for the otherwise lackluster Abu Dhabi. They sell unlimited tickets resulting in 3-4 hrs of waittimes for the main rides and 30mins - 1.5 hrs wait times for all the other decent ones. A full days pass of 375 AED and you are lucky enough to get in 3 rides all day. Not to mention it's a weekday and I'm terrified of what the waittimes are on the weekends.

Ferrari World simply sucks and is overhyped. Please look into other better options like the other theme parks in Dubai. Surely, you might not have the World's fastest coaster but you can enjoy a slightly slower coaster multiple times and get great bang for your buck.

Edit: The cafes inside are overpriced compared to anywhere on the yas island. You're better off entering the yas mall food court for good food. Not to mention there are wait times of upto 1 hr to place your food order in a few joints inside. The main rollercoaster was closed for about an hour for 'maintenance' extending the wait time to approximately 5 hrs. You're better off spending your money and time elsewhere in UAE, there is plenty more to see here

If you are gonna come to Ferrari World, make sure you come in the middle of summer when there is no one around. But again, there is no guarantee that the money hungry folks of FW will have the main attractions working.

We bought 3 General Admission tickets. All fast tracks were sold out. Most rides had posted wait times of 2 to 3.5 hours each. My dad refused to spend the whole day in lines and ended up leaving.

My brother and I decided to try anyway. We waited 2 hours for one ride and did get on it, but after that we agreed it wasn’t worth it and left too. While we were there, we also watched a different ride (posted at a 2-hour wait) break down, and it stayed down for a long time with no clear handling or updates from staff.

Ferrari is selling a stand in line experience. Not worth it. Our recommendation is to avoid this park.

reviews.text:
Ferrari World Abu Dhabi is a dream destination for speed junkies and automotive enthusiasts alike. One of the best parts of the experience is that the entire park is indoors, providing a comfortable, climate-controlled environment to enjoy world-class thrills regardless of the weather outside.

The absolute standout ride is Formula Rossa. As the fastest roller coaster in the world, its lightning-fast acceleration is something you have to feel to believe; it is truly the ultimate adrenaline rush.

For those seeking sheer intensity, Flying Aces is incredibly thrilling, featuring one of the world's highest roller coaster loops.

I also highly recommend Mission Ferrari, which stands out as a brilliantly interactive and immersive roller coaster that blends physical drops with high-tech storytelling.

Even the Turbo track provides a great ride, adding to the variety of the park.

Beyond the heart-pounding attractions, the atmosphere is elevated by the stunning display of Ferrari car models. Seeing the evolution and craftsmanship of these iconic machines up close makes the visit all the more impressive. Whether you are there for the record-breaking speeds or the Italian luxury, Ferrari World is a top-tier attraction that shouldn't be missed.
reviews.author: Anand Gupta

reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointing Experience – Total Waste of Money

I had one of the worst theme park experiences of my life at Ferrari World Abu Dhabi, and I strongly regret coming here.

I visited with my family who came all the way to Dubai to see me, including my young siblings who were extremely excited about Ferrari World. I spent over 2,200 AED just on tickets, expecting a world-class experience. What no one tells you — and what should be clearly mentioned — is that waiting times are absolutely insane: 2 to 5 HOURS per ride.

When we arrived, all fast pass tickets were already sold out. I went to the information desk and politely asked if they could help us with just TWO fast pass tickets for my young siblings, explaining that they might never get the chance to visit again. The answer was a flat NO, no empathy, no effort to help, nothing.

As a result, we managed to ride only ONE roller coaster after waiting 2.5 hours. When we tried to go to other rides, the queues were 3 to 4 hours long. This is completely unacceptable and honestly insane for a paid attraction at this price level.

My younger siblings were heartbroken and disappointed, and as a family we felt cheated. This place is severely overcrowded, clearly with no limit on the number of people allowed inside, and the management seems to care only about selling tickets, not about visitor experience.

Unless you buy fast pass tickets WELL IN ADVANCE, do NOT come here. Otherwise, you will spend your entire day standing in lines and walking around doing nothing.

Ironically, the best time to visit is probably summer, because right now it feels like they are just taking people’s money for nothing. For the price paid, this experience was absolutely not worth it.

I do NOT recommend Ferrari World to anyone without fast pass tickets. Save your money or go somewhere that actually values its guests.

reviews.text:
It's a straight up money printing machine to make up for the otherwise lackluster Abu Dhabi. They sell unlimited tickets resulting in 3-4 hrs of waittimes for the main rides and 30mins - 1.5 hrs wait times for all the other decent ones. A full days pass of 375 AED and you are lucky enough to get in 3 rides all day. Not to mention it's a weekday and I'm terrified of what the waittimes are on the weekends.

Ferrari World simply sucks and is overhyped. Please look into other better options like the other theme parks in Dubai. Surely, you might not have the World's fastest coaster but you can enjoy a slightly slower coaster multiple times and get great bang for your buck.

Edit: The cafes inside are overpriced compared to anywhere on the yas island. You're better off entering the yas mall food court for good food. Not to mention there are wait times of upto 1 hr to place your food order in a few joints inside. The main rollercoaster was closed for about an hour for 'maintenance' extending the wait time to approximately 5 hrs. You're better off spending your money and time elsewhere in UAE, there is plenty more to see here

If you are gonna come to Ferrari World, make sure you come in the middle of summer when there is no one around. But again, there is no guarantee that the money hungry folks of FW will have the main attractions working.

reviews.text:
Al Hudayriat Island has quickly become one of my favourite places in Abu Dhabi. It’s the kind of destination where you feel an instant shift the moment you arrive — open spaces, wide skies, and that refreshing island breeze that makes everything feel lighter. Whether you’re going for a walk, a bike ride, or just a peaceful break from the city, the whole area feels thoughtfully designed and beautifully maintained.

The beach is clean and spacious, with stunning views, soft sand, and plenty of room to relax without feeling crowded. I love how the island blends nature with modern facilities: cafés, food trucks, sports areas, running and cycling tracks, and shaded seating all come together so effortlessly. It’s family-friendly, active-friendly, and perfect for solo visits too.

What really stands out is the atmosphere — calm, uplifting, and full of life at the same time. You see people exercising, families enjoying the beach, friends gathering for a casual evening, and it all adds to the energy of the place. It’s one of the rare spots that truly offers something for everyone.

Whether you want an active day or a quiet escape, Al Hudayriat Island delivers every time. A must-visit in Abu Dhabi.

reviews.text: We stayed at this hotel for a few days and overall our experience was very positive.||The hotel is located on Saadiyat Island, not far from the airport and still reasonably close to Abu Dhabi city. Even though it is on an island, it is easy to reach points of interest and go out during the day. The beach itself is very long and shared by several resorts, and we felt that Jumeirah probably has one of the most organized and direct accesses to the sea.||The hotel is in excellent condition. Everything feels new, very clean and well organized. The layout of the building is a bit unusual, so moving around between rooms, common areas and facilities is not always very intuitive and sometimes a little inconvenient; also you don’t feel a lot the arabian style or influence. Still, the property is beautiful and clearly very well maintained.||There three swimming pools. They are not very large, but to be honest they almost don’t matter once you see the sea. The real highlight of this hotel is without any doubt the beach on Saadiyat Island. During our stay the sea was slightly rough, but still incredibly beautiful. We were told that in other periods of the year it is calmer and perfect for swimming and spending long hours in the water. In our opinion, it is one of the most beautiful beaches we have seen in the UAE and definitely the strongest point of this resort.|We would also like to mention the beach staff, especially Noel and Shetty, who were always kind, helpful and attentive, making our time by the sea even more enjoyable.||The rooms also deserve a special mention. They are spacious, modern and impeccably clean. Housekeeping was excellent and we really have nothing negative to say about room comfort or cleanliness.|Service throughout the hotel is outstanding. The staff are extremely professional, always smiling, punctual and very attentive. This level of service is not easy to find, and here it truly feels like top-quality hospitality.||We tried several dining options during our stay. The buffet restaurant offered good quality food. The buffet is not huge, but it is well organized and fairly varied, with some sections, such as Indian cuisine or dishes with a Russian influence, changing from evening to evening. Overall, a good standard.|Breakfast was also very pleasant, and we would like to thank Saqlain and Shan, who were always friendly, welcoming and attentive, and really made the start of our day nicer.|We also had dinner at the Italian restaurant and were pleasantly surprised: the food was very good, the ingredients were high quality and it felt close to what you would expect from a solid, authentic Italian restaurant. The Middle Eastern restaurant was excellent as well, both in terms of food quality and atmosphere, and the service was great.||One small thing to keep in mind is that there is not much natural shade on the beach. Vegetation is limited, with only a few palm trees here and there, so if you are looking for lots of shade and greenery, this might not be the ideal place. That said, everything is still perfectly manageable and comfortable.

reviews.text:
Dear Jumeirah Saadiyat Island hotel l Management Team,

I am an Emirati citizen from Abu Dhabi, and I would like to formally raise a complaint regarding an incident that occurred during my visit to your hotel on 13/12. I had a confirmed restaurant reservation at 5:30 PM, and I arrived at the hotel with my guests and my children, one of whom is a child with autism.

Before dining, we took a short walk and sat facing the beach, which was already crowded with visitors. During this time, an assistant security officer approached us and informed us that we were not allowed to sit facing the sea or allow our children to play on the sand, solely because we had not booked a hotel room — despite having a valid restaurant reservation within the hotel.

When we attempted to discuss the matter calmly and respectfully, the head of security arrived and reiterated the same instructions in a firm manner, stating that we were not permitted to remain and that we had to leave the area.

At that time, there were only approximately 30 minutes remaining before our dinner reservation. I fail to understand how quietly sitting by the sea with our children during this short period could have negatively affected the general atmosphere, particularly when the beach was already full of visitors wearing far less appropriate attire.

There was a clear sense of discrimination in the way we were treated, especially considering that we were Emirati guests wearing abayas. This raises serious concerns about selective enforcement of policies and whether our removal was based on objective rules or on our nationality and modest appearance.

It is also important to highlight that the discussion took place in front of other guests, including visitors from the Gulf region, who could clearly hear the exchange. Is this reflective of a hotel that claims to uphold a welcoming and respectful environment for all guests, or should such matters be handled privately and discreetly?

Furthermore, I would like to ask whether it is acceptable to prevent children of determination from playing on the sand, supposedly to preserve a certain image of the beach. I would like to reiterate that my son is a child with autism, and this situation was both upsetting and deeply disappointing for our family.

I believe this experience reflects a lack of cultural sensitivity, inclusivity, and respect, which does not align with the hospitality values and national principles upheld in the United Arab Emirates.

I respectfully request a formal explanation and clarification of the policy that was applied, as well as an explanation of how and why it was enforced in this manner.

Sincerely,
Aysha

reviews.text:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Une expérience exceptionnelle – Le meilleur hôtel de Saadiyat Island

J’ai récemment séjourné au Jumeirah Saadiyat Island, et je peux affirmer sans hésitation qu’il s’agit du meilleur hôtel de l’île. Dès l’arrivée, on ressent immédiatement le sens du service, la qualité des infrastructures et l’attention portée aux moindres détails.

Un point mérite d’être particulièrement souligné : le professionnalisme et la gentillesse de Florian Toczkowski. Sa disponibilité, sa bienveillance et sa capacité à anticiper les besoins des clients font véritablement la différence. Grâce à lui, chaque interaction devient fluide, chaleureuse et personnalisée. C’est rare de rencontrer un responsable qui combine à ce point efficacité, empathie et élégance dans le service.

Les infrastructures sont tout simplement impeccables :
•	Chambres spacieuses et parfaitement entretenues, literie extrêmement confortable, équipements modernes et ambiance apaisante.
•	Espaces communs lumineux et élégants, parfaitement pensés pour la détente et le bien-être.
•	Propreté irréprochable dans l’ensemble de l’hôtel : chaque zone, de la plage aux restaurants, reflète un niveau d’exigence remarquable.
•	Plage magnifique, sable fin, eau cristalline et installations de qualité (transats, parasols, service plage attentif). C’est l’un des plus beaux cadres de Saadiyat.
•	Installations sportives et bien-être de haut niveau, avec des équipes toujours respectueuses, souriantes et très professionnelles.

Ce qui frappe le plus, au-delà de l’infrastructure, c’est le respect et la courtoisie des équipes. Chaque employé, quel que soit son rôle, adopte une attitude exemplaire. On sent une culture du service profondément ancrée, ce qui rend le séjour encore plus agréable.

En résumé : un hôtel sublime, un service irréprochable, une plage exceptionnelle et une équipe qui place la barre très haut. Une adresse incontournable pour ceux qui recherchent tranquillité, confort et excellence sur Saadiyat Island.

Je recommande sans aucune réserve.

reviews.text:
Это наш третий пляжный отель на Садияте, так что мне есть с чем сравнить.
1) Длинная пляжная линия и всего в 2 ряда. Приятно что вам будет доступно сразу 4 лежака, что напомнило мне пляжные клубы в Форте дей Марми. Это действительно удобно и не создается ощущения толпы. Кстати за время пребывания в отеле всем хватало места на первой линии у воды, даже некоторые места были пустые.
2) Номера просторные как и в других отелях поблизости. У нас был номер с видом на воду и за счет удачного расположения всех корпусов, вид приятнее чем в других отелях на этом берегу. Уборка 2 раза, из приятного — оставляют маленькие шоколадки после вечерней уборки и крем после солнца. Предоставляют 6 бутылок воды, так что жажда вас не замучает (многим другим отелям следовало бы взять пример)
3) На территории есть 3 приятных ресторана где мы проводили ужины. Особенно понравился SDL и их менеджмент, сделали для нас маленькое исключение чем очень порадовали. Что касается буфета (шведского стола), то завтраки однообразные, а ужин проводить там совсем не хотелось. При этом буфет не плохой, это просто мои предпочтения.
4) Классный спорт зал. Зона силового тренинга отличная, гантели до 40кг, тренажеры и оборудование technogym (включая зону кардио). Зал оцениваю на 5/5.
5) Великолепный персонал и гостеприимство. Искренне чувствовалась забота и радушие. Я бы хотел узнать больше как менеджмент этого добился. Я в восторге.
6) Отель хорошо подходит для отдыха с детьми (включая малышей до 2 лет)

Что можно было бы улучшить:
1) Я удивлен что пишу это, но мне показалось что фруктовый лед на пляже разносят крайне редко. Не то чтобы я фанат фруктового льда, но в жару он приятно освежает. И вкус всего один, за неделю манго надоел)
2) Сотрудник который ходит по пляжу и предлагает обновить солнцезащитный крем и протереть очки — на мой взгляд это лишнее. Возможно я скромный, но это такие простейшие операции что мне было жаль что другой человек тратит на это время своей жизни.

Во всем остальном это отличный отель, но то из-за чего бы я вернулся сюда еще раз — гостеприимство сотрудников. Спасибо вам 🤝

The whole experience felt calm and grounding. The moment I arrived I noticed how quiet the place is no chaos, no loud crowds, just the sound of the sea and birds. It gave me this weird mix of peace and nostalgia.

The beach is unreal the water is so clear it doesn’t even look real. I spent a lot of time just walking barefoot on the sand and somehow it felt almost therapeutic. It’s the kind of place where you suddenly slow down without trying.

The hotel itself is beautiful without being “too much.” Natural tones, clean design, lots of space and light. I loved the small details cold towels, the scent in the lobby, and how everyone speaks softly like they know you came here to reset.

The staff were kind. They check on you but never in a way that interrupts your quiet moment.

This hotel calls itself a 5-star luxury beach hotel. It’s true that the view from the rooms, the pool area, and the beach are amazing. Unfortunately that’s where the “luxury” ends. The service is poor, particularly at the front desk and from housekeeping. The front desk went out of their way to make life difficult for us at check-in. The housekeepers appear at random times of day offering to clean the room, even when this is clearly not wanted nor requested. When you dial 4343 to order room service, the phone rings unanswered for several minutes before you finally get through to someone who clearly doesn’t know the menu. It’s odd that a supposed five-star hotel would have a buffet restaurant which would feel more at home in a budget four-star in Benidorm. That said, the food and service at the Italian restaurant on the beach was excellent.

Overall this nowhere near lived up to the hype. I would avoid it and stay at the St Regis or Park Hyatt instead, which have the same incredible beachfront views but with far higher standards of service.

My partner and I traveled all the way from Dubai to dine at La Cava, following a glowing recommendation and it did not disappoint. From the moment we stepped into the venue, it was clear this was going to be a special night.

The food? Absolutely insane. Every dish we tried was bursting with flavor. Whether you're a seasoned foodie or just love good Spanish food, La Cava delivers a culinary experience that exceeds expectations.

And the wine... what a selection. No matter which bottle you choose, you’re in for a treat. The wine list is top-tier, and what makes it even better is the staff’s knowledge — they clearly know and love what they’re serving. We especially appreciated the guidance we got from the team when picking our pairings.

A special mention must go to Paolo, the manager, whose warmth, professionalism, and attention to detail took the experience to another level. The entire service team was exceptional, friendly, and genuinely passionate.

To top it all off, we happened to visit on a flamenco night. The live Spanish music, the vibrant yet relaxed atmosphere, and the beautiful venue itself made the evening unforgettable.

Highly recommended to anyone who appreciates great food, outstanding wine, and unforgettable ambience.

reviews.text:
La Cava is a attractive restaurant/wine bar located both on the ground level and wine cellar inside the Rosewood Hotel.  The wine cellar is hidden away down a spiral staircase.  Descending down the stairs, you feel as though you are being ushered to a secretive or exclusive hip hotspot.

My wife and I first visited La Cava about a week ago.  It was around 6 pm and we had the place to ourselves.  Our server was incredibly attentive, funny, and well-spoken.  He explained to us about about the 7 to 9 Grape & Cheese special, which we booked for later in the week when were leaving.  The music being played during this visit was pure classic jazz and truly fit the intimate setting of the cellar.  He explained that the Grape & Cheese nights were very popular and that the cellar would get very noisy and that we should take a look at the available seating upstairs.

We opted to reserve seating on the ground floor level for the next visit.  The area is nice and seating is spread out making it perfect when wanting to have a conversation.  This worked out perfectly when we had a guest join us for this evening.  The only issue was that the initial seating we had was really uncomfortable.  Our server quickly showed us to another area which was better.

He got our evening off with some bubbly and plates of finely sliced meats, an assortment of breads, and several types of cheese.  As the evening celebration unfolded we sampled a very nice Pinot Noir and a delectable dry Riesling.  With great conversation and wines flowing our two hours came to a end much quicker than expected.  Time seriously flew by...  Each night we have been there, the staff on hand has made us feel welcomed and well cared for.  The snacks have been delightful and scrumptious, and the setting transports one to Bordeaux or Tuscany.  La Cava is a place we look forward to taking many an extended vacation to in the months to come.

reviews.text: Honestly disappointing! We came here based on good reviews from our friends, but from booking all the way to leaving, our experience was terrible. Every other table was catered for except for ours. I guess when you book at La Cava don't use an Arabic name! Also, the selection of cold cuts wasn't the best, but the Cheeses were good. I would rather go to Spacanapoli next time!

reviews.text:
It could be great...

There are some wonderful exhibits and pieces to see/experience, the curators have done an exceptional job bringing together an eclectic mix of works from across multiple periods with global reference.  The spaces are in the main light and easy to move around, the modern-era galleries however were freezing cold compared to the rest, making it a little uncomfortable.
There is plenty of space outside to rest and relax and take in the bizarre spectacle of people walking the dock.

However;
The wayfinding signage is effectively non-existent, whilst the layout of exhibits is confused making it occasionally difficult to identify where the path for each room starts.
Especially in the first spaces, the information signs on the floor are almost unreadable due to their location, especially when it's busy, whilst in the remainder of the galleries there is really not much information shared for each piece.
The gallery introduction text is illogically placed, in most spaces it is effectively behind you and easily missed.
The guided talk via the app contains numerous basic pronunciation errors, and serves to provide little additional information beyond that on the introduction passages and piece descriptions.  When it is busy, as it was when we visited, it doesn't feel comfortable to be able to try to read information boards as people push past or are otherwise 'instagramming' their way through life, so the lack of audio information was a little disappointing.
There are no places to sit and observe the pieces as you would in a typical gallery/museum space, especially those of scale, whilst the prohibitive security controls (whilst assuredly required to cater to the lowest denominator of visitor) preclude what is a fairly standard practice of note-taking and observational sketching/drawing in other places.

Overall Louvre Abu Dhabi is well worth a visit, and upcoming exhibitions will certainly be visited, however it's a shame that the overall experience caters more to those who want to say they have been, rather than those who truly want to experience the pieces and the space.

reviews.text:
Bu müzeyi grup turuyla ziyaret ettim. Dubai ve Abu Dabi’deki her şey gibi bu bina, harika bir zevk ve modern mimari sergiliyor. Burası Louvre adını kullanıyor ancak orijinaliyle rekabet etmeyi düşünmüyor. Sergiler çoğunlukla heykellerdir, ancak sergilerin düzenlemesi gözüme çok hoş geliyor. Akşam saatlerinde vardık ve onu görmek için yalnızca 2 saatimiz vardı. O yüzden kız arkadaşım ve ben hızımızı hızlandırdık ve oradaki her şeyi hızlı bir tempoda bile hayranlıkla izleyebildik.
Büyüleyici sergiler, sizi dünyanın farklı bölgelerini birbirine bağlayan, asırlarca süren bir arazi gezintisine çıkarır. Ekranların çoğu etkileşimliydi ve bu da deneyimi iyileştirdi.

Mamluklar, 1250-1517 yılları arasında büyülüydü; yükselmelerini, sanatları, kültürleri ve mirasıyla tarihe nasıl etki ettiğini gösteriyorlardı.

Biletler makul fiyatlıydı ve fiyatına kıyasla yüksek değer verdiğimi düşündüm. Kafe, hak ettiğiniz bir mola veriyor ve hediyelik eşya dükkânı hediyelik eşyalarla dolu. Otobüs veya taksi kullanmak çok kolay.

Personel cana yakın, yardımsever ve bilgili. Gezginlerin, farklı kültürlerin ve bölgelerin sanat ve tasarım yoluyla nasıl bir araya geldiğine dair bilgi edinmek için burayı ziyaret etmelerini tavsiye ederim.

reviews.text:
It could be great...

There are some wonderful exhibits and pieces to see/experience, the curators have done an exceptional job bringing together an eclectic mix of works from across multiple periods with global reference.  The spaces are in the main light and easy to move around, the modern-era galleries however were freezing cold compared to the rest, making it a little uncomfortable.
There is plenty of space outside to rest and relax and take in the bizarre spectacle of people walking the dock.

However;
The wayfinding signage is effectively non-existent, whilst the layout of exhibits is confused making it occasionally difficult to identify where the path for each room starts.
Especially in the first spaces, the information signs on the floor are almost unreadable due to their location, especially when it's busy, whilst in the remainder of the galleries there is really not much information shared for each piece.
The gallery introduction text is illogically placed, in most spaces it is effectively behind you and easily missed.
The guided talk via the app contains numerous basic pronunciation errors, and serves to provide little additional information beyond that on the introduction passages and piece descriptions.  When it is busy, as it was when we visited, it doesn't feel comfortable to be able to try to read information boards as people push past or are otherwise 'instagramming' their way through life, so the lack of audio information was a little disappointing.
There are no places to sit and observe the pieces as you would in a typical gallery/museum space, especially those of scale, whilst the prohibitive security controls (whilst assuredly required to cater to the lowest denominator of visitor) preclude what is a fairly standard practice of note-taking and observational sketching/drawing in other places.

Overall Louvre Abu Dhabi is well worth a visit, and upcoming exhibitions will certainly be visited, however it's a shame that the overall experience caters more to those who want to say they have been, rather than those who truly want to experience the pieces and the space.

We went to Louvre Abu Dhabi, an annex of the Louvre Museum in Paris.
The surrounding area was crowded, but once inside the museum it wasn't so noticeable and I was able to enjoy the exhibits at my own pace.

It's not as large as the Louvre in France,
but there are a fair number of exhibits, so it will take some time to see everything.
Photography is permitted inside the museum.

We didn't have much time so we left after about an hour, but honestly it was a shame.
It's best to buy your tickets online in advance.
They're a little cheaper and allow for smoother entry.
reviews.author: Rei

reviews.text:
The Louvre at Abu Dhabi is really only for those who are seriously interested in history, art, and most importantly, have the patience to read all the name plates and descriptions.

If not, it is a short walk through a very modern looking building that literally sits on the sea. There were some gorgeous, ancient sculptures, paintings, and even jewellery. There were so many ancient pieces from long dead civilizations with the only exception being the pieces from the Indian civilization (meaning the Indian civilization is the only one that survived to modern day). There were also more relatively contemporary works from the last 500 years.

reviews.text:
The Louvre Abu Dhabi is a beautifully designed museum with a clean, post-modern layout. The iconic steel dome is both striking and practical — a perfect parasol under the sun. The experience feels immersive, with thoughtfully curated displays that guide you smoothly through history.

Highlights for me were the bulla, the statue of Ramses II, and the paintings of the Virgin Mary and other Christian relics — truly exquisite pieces. The museum connects cultures and eras effortlessly, making it both engaging and meaningful.

A must-visit in Abu Dhabi. Elegant, inspiring and genuinely memorable. 🏛️✨
